content: Phendimetrazine is a medication prescribed as part of a comprehensive weight-loss program that includes a doctor-approved exercise regimen, behavioral changes, and a reduced-calorie diet. It is specifically used for individuals who are overweight, particularly those classified as obese or those with weight-related medical conditions. The exact mechanism by which this medication aids in weight loss is not fully understood. However, it is believed to work by suppressing appetite, increasing energy expenditure, or influencing certain areas of the brain. How to Use: The immediate-release form of phendimetrazine should be taken orally as directed by your doctor, typically 2 to 3 times daily, one hour before meals. The sustained-release form is usually taken once daily, 30 to 60 minutes before the morning meal. Swallow the medication whole. Do not crush, chew, or break the capsules. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. Your doctor will adjust the dose to find the most effective amount for you. Use this medication regularly and exactly as prescribed to achieve the best results. It is generally prescribed for short-term use, typically a few weeks at a time. Do not take this medication with other appetite suppressants unless directed by your doctor. Withdrawal and Dependency: Abruptly stopping this medication may lead to withdrawal symptoms such as depression or severe fatigue. To prevent withdrawal, your doctor may gradually reduce your dose. Withdrawal is more likely if you have been using phendimetrazine for an extended period or at high doses. This medication has the potential for addiction, particularly in individuals with a history of substance use disorders (e.g., overuse of or addiction to drugs or alcohol). Do not increase your dose, take it more frequently, or use it for a longer duration than prescribed. Side Effects: Common side effects include dizziness, dry mouth, difficulty sleeping, irritability, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or constipation. This medication may raise your blood pressure. Rarely, it can cause serious and potentially fatal lung or heart problems, such as pulmonary hypertension or heart valve issues. The risk increases with prolonged use or when combined with other appetite suppressants or herbal products. A severe allergic reaction to this medication is rare but possible. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience symptoms of an allergic reaction. Precautions: Before taking phendimetrazine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or other sympathomimetic amines (e.g., pseudoephedrine, amphetamines, phentermine) or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause dizziness, blurred vision, or, in rare cases, drowsiness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness or clear vision until you can do so safely. Avoid alcoholic beverages. If you have diabetes, monitor your blood sugar levels regularly and share the results with your doctor. This medication should not be used during pregnancy, as weight loss offers no benefit to a pregnant woman and may harm the unborn baby. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk, but similar drugs do. Breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Avoid using this medication with certain drugs, such as MAO inhibitors (e.g., isocarboxazid, phenelzine, tranylcypromine), as serious and potentially fatal interactions may occur. Most MAO inhibitors should not be taken for two weeks before or after treatment with this medication. Check the labels of all your medications (e.g., allergy or cough-and-cold products) as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness or increase your heart rate or blood pressure. Caffeine can also amplify the side effects of this medication. Overdose: In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Notes: Appetite suppressants should not replace a proper diet. Do not share this medication with others. Regular lab and medical tests (e.g., blood pressure, heart, and kidney function) may be conducted while you are taking this medication. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose or late in the evening, skip the missed dose. Take your next dose at the regular time. Storage: Store at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This summary does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
